n eval run of an existing suite, or upload a versioned suite file and run it. Provide **either** `--suite` **or** `--file`, not bo
th.\n\nBy default the command prints a launch receipt and returns immediately. `--wait` polls every launched run to a terminal sta
te.\n\n**Exit codes (`--wait` only).** Without `--wait` this command's exit code is unchanged: `0` on any launch, `1` on a partial
or wholly failed fan-out. `--wait` owns a separate six-code contract — a caller who asked this process to sit and watch a run to

completion is asking it to say how the run went:

| Code | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `0` | Every waited run passed, unanimously, a
nd (when a report was requested) every report was assembled |\n| `1` | A run **completed** with a **failed** verdict. The only con
dition that produces this code |\n| `2` | Usage error — bad flags, `--reporter`/`--out` without `--wait`, or an invalid suite file
(after auth, before any server/model work) |\n| `3` | Auth failed — no credential, or the platform rejected it, at launch or mid-
wait (a token that expired during a long poll). Zero credits spent if it happened before launch |\n| `4` | Connection/setup failed
before evaluation — a launch failure this CLI itself observed (network, timeout, rate limit, a partial or failed fan-out, an unre
cognized launch error), or a local `--out` write failure — unless a more severe outcome (`1` or `3`) already applies to the same r
un, per the merge order above |\n| `5` | No valid verdict — `inconclusive`, a null/unrecognized result, a run whose own status is
failed/cancelled/timed-out, a wait that hit its deadline, a mid-wait failure that was not auth-shaped, or a report that could not
be assembled |\n\nNo infrastructure condition ever maps to `1` — see the same rule under `eval gate` below. A multi-target launch
merges these worst-of across every waited run, in the order `1 > 3 > 4 > 5 > 0`: a real verdict failure is never masked by a sibli
ng's infrastructure noise, and a credential failure (which may be *why* other targets show no verdict) outranks a plain connection
failure.\n\nThis six-code contract is new and deliberately **different** from `eval gate`'s four codes below — see that command's
own doc for why the two are not unified. An invalid suite file exits **2** either way — `eval validate` still exits 1 for the sam

e contract failure, because it is a verdict on the file and this command is not.

| Flag | Required | Description |
| - | - | -
|\n| `--suite <id-or-name>` | Yes, unless `--file` | Eval suite name or ID |\n| `--file <path>` | Yes, unless `--suite` | Version
ed suite file to upload and run (`.yaml` or `.json`, or `-` for stdin) |\n| `--project <id-or-name>` | No | Project name or ID (de
faults to the most recently updated project) |\n| `--server <id-or-name...>` | No | Override the suite's saved server selection (H
TTP servers only) |\n| `--environment <id-or-name...>` | No | Attached project environment(s) to run. Several values start one **p
aid run each**. |\n| `--client <id-or-name...>` | No | Attached client(s) to run, so the run is stamped with that client's config.
Several values start one **paid run each**. |\n| `--host <id-or-name...>` | No | **Deprecated** alias for `--client`. Passing bot
h is an error. Not the host-compat catalog id `mcpjam compat --host` / `mcpjam tools --host` take — see [Two different `--host` fl
ags](#two-different---host-flags). |\n| `--all-targets` | No | Run **every** attached environment (or, if none, every attached hos
t) — one **paid run per target** |\n| `--iterations <n>` | No | Run each case this many times (1-10), for this run only |\n| `--re
petitions <n>` | No | **Legacy** spelling of `--iterations`. Passing both is an error. |\n| `--case <id-or-title...>` | No | Run o
nly these cases instead of the whole suite |\n| `--exclude-skills` | No | Run the \"without skills\" A/B arm: nothing is pinned, a
nd the run is labelled as excluded |\n| `--refresh-snapshot` | No | **Persists a new host-config snapshot on the suite** (see belo
w). Single-target runs only. |", "is_error": false}]}, "parent_tool_use_id": null, "session_id": "280d3384-ab57-43a6-8e6e-dc432763
